dispositions.method: The automatic families first printed in 1779 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json: 625 items printed somewhere; by the finder's count 4 reach 7 papers, 11 reach 6, 60 reach 5 and 156 reach 4). The same script was run with year 1778 over the 1779 pages (items_from_1778.json: 16 items, none in more than 3 papers). Every finder item in 3 or more papers (496) was counted again by its own opening against every page of 1779 in both transcriptions: first by about 100 words, then, because a short item's 100 words take in the paragraph printed after it, by the first 40 words (a page prints the item when it holds at least 18 of the opening's word 5-grams). Items read from different printings of one text were merged, and the parts of one document joined (a letter with the enclosures printed with it, a day's resolutions of Congress under one heading, an address printed in parts). A sweep of the year for passages shared word for word (seven-word sequences) by 4 or more papers, as the 1803 review introduced (X-1803-09), found short items the reuse families had not joined; each was counted by its own opening. The 30 chosen items were then counted by their openings with phrase searches over all 1,660 pages of 1779 in both transcriptions, and every hit was read.
dispositions.selection_rule: The thin-year rule (Y-THIN), as amended by the owner on 23 November 2026 (choice B1): an item, counted by its own words, is eligible when it was printed by more than half of the newspapers that survive for its weeks (those with a surviving issue between its first and last printing, and at least in the three weeks from its first printing), and by at least 4; items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted; the other eligible items are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news, about as many stories as a standard year (about 20 to 35, a target, not a quota); digests are not admitted. One item of 1779 is printed by every surviving paper: the King's speech of 26 November 1778 (7 of 7). From the other eligible items 29 were chosen, in 26 stories (two parents with five groups), covering every month and the kinds of news of the year (the war in America; Congress, the currency and public life; Britain, Spain and the war at sea). Where several items of one affair reach the bar in the same weeks, the most widely printed is chosen and the others are listed as not chosen, unless they are separate public acts (X-1800-01): General Washington's two letters on Stony Point and the thanks of Congress are three public acts. Nothing is held back for its subject.
dispositions.paper_counting: 1779 has 9 catalogue series, which are 9 papers: no paper is under two catalogue numbers. The Pennsylvania Packet (Philadelphia, three a week), the New-York Gazette, and the Weekly Mercury (New York, held by the British; Mondays), the Connecticut Courant (Hartford; Tuesdays), the New-Jersey Gazette (Trenton; Wednesdays) and the New-Hampshire Gazette (Portsmouth; Tuesdays) run all year; the Virginia Gazette (Williamsburg) from 12 February; the Newport Gazette (Newport, held by the British) on 25 March and from 1 July to 6 October; the New-Jersey Journal (Chatham) and the Gazette of the State of South-Carolina (Charlestown) have one issue each (16 February, 15 September). Papers in print in any three weeks: 5 in January, 6 or 7 from February to July, 7 or 8 in August and September, 6 from October; the bar is 4 papers almost all year and 5 where an item's weeks hold both the Newport Gazette and the South Carolina issue. Every count here counts eligible pages of issues the release dates to 1779.
